title: GameSpec v1.0
description: The hand-off contract of the MAAEGDE six-agent accounting educational game design pipeline. Every field carries x-agent: the single agent that owns it. Derived fields (x-derived: true) are computed by the validator and MUST NOT be authored.

audience.description: named learner level, e.g. 'undergraduate managerial accounting, post-lecture'

outOfScope.description: The framework states in its own data what it does not cover. Used to keep coverage claims honest.

sources.description: Every authority.ref and every dataset.provenance must resolve to an id here.

archivedAt.description: path or URL of the pinned copy

objectives.description: THE SPINE. Every graded step references at least one objective id; the validator derives assessedBy and refuses a spec that authors it.

kind.description: ethics / professional-judgement objectives are exempt from authority.ref patterns; see assurance.authorityPolicy.

maxChanceScore.description: guessing budget across this objective's assessing steps

competencyRef.description: optional external map: AACSB / CPA blueprint / course LO code

taxonomy.description: Optional: a checklist the game teaches as a SET (the six internal-control activities; the three regression-validity criteria). Drives checklist UI and debrief rollup.

modes.description: Cross-cutting play modes (solo vs class-competition). A first-class construct because mode is not a local override: in acc214-cost-estimation it touches four agents' field sets at 13 sites.

affects.description: Every field path this mode changes. The validator cross-checks that each path exists and that its owning agent is recorded in provenance.

knowledge.description: THE CHOKEPOINT. Every number a student is graded against enters the spec exactly once, here, owned by one agent. Agents 3 and 4 may only reference it. This single rule is what makes Agent 5 arithmetic checks portable to any game instead of eleven hand-written closures keyed to case ids.

params.description: Named numeric/string primitives. Referenced from prose as {{p.name}}.

thresholds.description: Every constant used in a gating, scoring or correctness expression. Undeclared magic numbers are an ERROR (check N6).

inclusive.description: whether comparisons against it are >= / <= (true) or > / < (false). Check N8 enforces one answer per threshold.

notDerivedFrom.description: REQUIRED when role is 'illustrative'. Names the dataset this one must NOT be read as a summary of. Closes the loophole where SPLIT_CANDIDATES totalling 40 observations sits next to a 10-row training table.

provenanceLabel.description: REQUIRED when role is 'illustrative'. Rendered on screen so a student sees it is not derived from the table just shown.

derivations.description: Named pure functions over declared datasets/params. Every displayed statistic must be reproducible by one of these (check N4).

artifacts.description: The evidence a student reads to answer. Unifies Document (markdown), ref/BILL_REF (invoice HTML), mini-ledger records, TRAINING_ROWS tables.

isDistractor.description: the red-herring flag, promoted to a first-class checked field

textAlternative.description: REQUIRED for exhibit-image. For a data-bearing image, also supply a machine-readable transcription so Agent 5 has something to check.

transcription.description: machine-readable content of a data-bearing exhibit-image

illustrativeNumbers.description: Declares that the figures in this artifact are illustrative samples, not values the answer key is derived from. Exempts it from check N2. Must be declared, never assumed — the point is that the exemption is visible in the spec.

scenario.description: ENTIRELY OPTIONAL. Decision Tree Builder Lab has no scenario and no persona; that is a design choice, not an omission, and the schema must be able to say so via framing: none.

voice.description: one line on how this character speaks; constrains generated dialogue

personas.description: Playable identity. selectionEffect names what choosing it actually does — the Case Game roles gate hints only, Cash Receipts roles are a replay matrix.

settings.description: Industry skin. contextualModifiers keyed by objectiveId.

beats.description: Narrative units. The Case Game BranchingEvent, Cost Estimation scene/outcome/simFail and Cash Receipts consequence interstitial all land here. CONSTRAINT (check C2): a beat may not introduce a number absent from knowledge.params or a declared derivation, unless flagged narrative:true — and a narrative:true quantifier carries an assertion obligation.

blocks.description: Typed rows, NOT pre-baked HTML. The corpus bakes HTML at author time via oRow(); the spec makes the emitter render it.

narrativeNumbers.description: Numbers in this beat that are deliberately not derived from knowledge. Each must declare a relation to the derived quantity sharing its unit.

objectiveIds.description: REQUIRED non-empty when graded is true (check P1)

taxonomyId.description: which taxonomy entry this step exercises

why.description: the reasoning shown after a correct answer

runtimeSemantics.description: Every optional mechanic declares active or inert. Authoring a field belonging to an inert mechanic is a WARN, not an ERROR: the Accounting Case Game ships 5 triggersEventId values, isRedHerring and roleRestriction that no code reads, and a schema that made that unexpressible could not use it as a fixture.

tree.description: Optional logical rule set, reused by traverse steps AND by assurance assertions. Exactly ONE executable definition; prose restatements are generated from it (check N7).

model.description: Five genuinely different strategies exist in the corpus, so this is a tagged union, not a number.

params.description: shape depends on model; validated by check S12

meters.description: A named non-score resource. trust (Cost Estimation 100->floor 20), risk (Cash Receipts start 22, clamp 0-100), streak, mastery. Score itself is just the distinguished meter.

affectsFinalGrade.description: REQUIRED by check S11. No defaults: the Case Game runs two different formulas over the same event (gameStore.ts:73 live HUD, uncapped; scoring.ts:10 grade, capped).

recordsAttempts.description: REQUIRED true when retryPolicy is until-correct-free, else the item statistics are uninterpretable (check Q3)

derivedCeilings.description: perfect-run score and perfect-run meter values, computed by the validator

feedback.description: Split into two objects so ownership is literally true. Gate order is POLICY BEFORE CONTENT: otherwise Agent 6 can only appeal after the fact.

oneOf.description: Cash Receipts: deferred-on-correct + interstitial-on-wrong, the most interesting timing in the corpus.

announceCost.description: Cost Estimation appends "(-half points)" only in competition mode, so solo players are never told the hint costs anything.

assertions.description: AUTHORED BEFORE READING flow/interaction — the audit program is written before the sample is drawn (gate order, mechanism C). Otherwise N1 is satisfiable by writing assertions the existing numbers already satisfy.

corpus.description: which text fields the recomputed value must appear in

writtenAtGate.description: the gate at which this assertion was authored; check N1b refuses assertions written after gate 5 opened the flow

attestation.description: Deliberately unautomatable. The validator proves internal consistency; only a person can confirm that a cited standard says what the answer claims.

notApplicable.description: Decision Tree Builder Lab uses this. An honest "no accounting content here" beats a fabricated ASC citation.

target.description: Pinned to dom for v1.0. Two independent extractions concluded a DOM target fixes real shipped defects for free: silently clipped chart bars, no per-button focus, hit-rects drifting from draw calls.

extensions.description: THE ESCAPE HATCH. Design rule: the RENDERING may be opaque, the PEDAGOGY never is. A widget can hide how it draws; it cannot hide what it assesses, what it awards, or whether a student can be judged by it.

fidelity.description: A widget used by exactly one game is bespoke-pending-generalisation, NOT registry-exact. Under the current corpus that is every widget: measured reuse factor is 1.0.

usedBy.description: game ids. Printed as a reuse factor in the build report so the registry claim stays falsifiable.

layout.description: opaque coordinate blob. Authored prose is FORBIDDEN here (check X5), which forces every authored string into an addressable content field.

fallback.description: MANDATORY and must itself be a fully valid generatable step. If the registry lacks the widget the emitter renders this and the build report says so. There is no silent drop.

earnedNotes.description: replay the feedback strings the student actually earned (the Cash Receipts debrief pattern)

provenance.description: RECORDS STATE, NOT SIGNATURES. A trail whose error field is constrained to zero can never evidence that any agent caught anything, and six signatures on one final document is exactly what a single author would emit.

profile.description: The genre profile is an explicit INPUT, recorded here, so profile-set fields are never attributed to an agent judgment.

hiddenFrom.description: field paths deliberately withheld from this agent (mechanism C: information hiding)

deltas.description: Every change to a field after its owner gate closed. The printed count of these IS the measurement of whether the sequence is load-bearing.

findings.description: Cross-agent catches as first-class objects. raisedBy != against is the only kind that evidences the pipeline.

slug.description: Identifier unique within its collection. camelCase is allowed because dataset column keys mirror the source data field names.

expr.description: restricted expression over knowledge.params, knowledge.derivations and step results. No function calls outside the declared derivation set.

note.description: REQUIRED for gaap-principle and professional-judgement: these have no citable Codification topic, and forcing an ASC number onto them is exactly the fabricated-precision failure Agent 5 exists to prevent.

consequence.description: Interstitial shown on a wrong pick. Check S3 is satisfied by feedback OR consequence: Cash Receipts deliberately ships "" feedback plus a real consequence string, and that is a design, not a defect.

misconceptionFormula.description: for numeric distractors: the wrong computation that produces this value (check N5)

consequence.description: Interstitial shown on a wrong pick. Check S3 is satisfied by feedback OR consequence: Cash Receipts deliberately ships "" feedback plus a real consequence string, and that is a design, not a defect.

misconceptionFormula.description: for numeric distractors: the wrong computation that produces this value (check N5)
